title: Development of a simple and versatile in vitro method for production, stimulation, and analysis of bioengineered muscle
author: Karen Wells-Cembrano
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b4qiqvue
materials: In this section, all steps are performed inside a biological safety cabinet (vertical flow / BSL-2 preferrable). Defrost myoblast cell line in a T75 flask and culture cells in their recommended maintenance medium. Human myoblasts must be passaged at a maximum of 60-70% confluence to avoid differentiation induced by cell-cell contacts. For maintenance of human myoblasts, we use Skeletal Muscle Cell Growth Medium PromoCell Catalog #C-23160 . Culture flasks are coated with a solution of 0.15% gelatin for 01:00:00 before use.

The day before the seeding, defrost the appropriate amount of Matrigel Growth Factor Reduced (GFR) Basement Membrane Matrix, LDEV-free Corning Catalog #356230 . For our experiments, a concentration of 7.2-8 mg/ml has been used with similar results. Leave aliquots on ice inside the fridge Overnight . It is recommended to start defrosting in the afternoon, and to change the ice the next morning.

Fluo-4 AM sterile stock solution should be prepared in advance at 1 millimolar (mM) in DMSO with 20 Mass / % volume Pluronic ® , and stored at -20ºC protected from light. To prepare the solvent, dissolve 2 g of Pluronic ® in 10 mL of sterile DMSO Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #D2650 . To increase solubility, leave the mixture in a 37 °C water bath for 00:20:00 min and vortex the solution until there are no more clumps of Pluronic ® . Then, filter this mixture at 0.22 μm in the biological safety hood. To reconstitute Fluo-4 AM, follow the manufacturer's instructions. Fluo-4, AM, cell permeant Thermo Fisher Catalog #F14217

Amplify cells to the needed amount. Take into account that around 3·10 6 cells are needed for each muscle bundle . If many replicates are to be seeded, a large number of flasks and high volume of cell culture medium may be necessary depending on the yield for each cell line. In the case of human myoblasts, cells are sometimes larger than other common cell lines, which can make it more difficult to obtain high yields of cells while keeping confluence under 70%. Make sure to become familiarized with the culture time and passage dilutions required for your specific muscle cell line, as well as usual yields of cells per T75 or T175 flask at ~70% confluence. This is necessary to ensure that the required number of cells will be available at the day of the experiment. For example, in our case, we obtain approximately 6 · 10 6 cells in one T175 flask. Therefore, we make sure to have at least one T175 at 70% confluence for every two replicates on the day of the experiment. We perform passages at a 1:5-1:10 dilution.
As a positive control of chemical stimulation, prepare a solution of 1 Molarity (M) KCl in Milli-Q TM H 2 O. It is not necessary to keep this solution sterile, although it may be filtered if desired.

On the day of stimulation, prepare a stock solution of acetylcholine in phenol red-free DMEM. Weigh the appropriate amount of acetylcholine chloride to prepare a 100X solution ( 10 millimolar (mM) ). For example, for 10 mL of stock solution, weigh 18.2 mg of Acetylcholine chloride Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #A6625 and add 10 mL of phenol red-free DMEM DMEM, high glucose, HEPES, no phenol red Thermo Fisher Catalog #21063029 . Finally, filter the solution with a 0.22 μm filter and store in the fridge until use. It is best to prepare the acetylcholine solution fresh, on the day that stimulation will be performed, to avoid degradation.

On the day of seeding, sterilize the necessary amount of Petri dishes according to the following steps. TIP: To the desired number of replicates, add at least two more Petri dishes for sterilization, which can be used as replacements in case one of the VELCRO ® pieces becomes detached during the sterilization process (this occurs in less than 10% of plates).

The day of the seeding, prepare a stock solution of fibrinogen at 8 mg/mL . Fibrinogen from bovine plasma Type I-S 65-85% protein (≥75% of protein is clottable) Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #F8630 . First, calculate the necessary amount of fibrinogen solution needed for your experiment, taking into account that 150 µL are needed for each muscle bundle. Prepare 1.5 times the necessary volume. Layer fibrinogen over warm (sterile) phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), leave it in the 37 °C water bath to fully dissolve (DO NOT VORTEX), and filter through a 0.22 μm filter. Keep the solution at 4 °C until use. It is best to prepare the fibrinogen solution fresh, as it only keeps for 4 °C .
Place the Petri dishes on larger (150 mm Ø or similar) Petri dishes, for ease of manipulation ( Figure 4 ). Add 70% ethanol to each dish, up to the brim, and leave for 00:15:00 .

Remove ethanol and wash 3 times with sterile PBS. Without removing the 3rd wash, leave the plates under UV light for 15 minutes (lid open and facing upwards as in Figure 4 ). Figure 4. Sterilization of plates with PBS under UV light.

After the plates have been dried in the incubator, perform coating with a sterile solution of 0.2 Mass / % volume Pluronic® F-127 Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #P2443 in Milli-Q ® water. This hydrophobic coating will facilitate detachment of the muscle bundles from the Petri dish. In order to coat only the middle region where the muscle bundle will be placed, and avoid soaking the velcro with a hydrophobic material, the Pluronic ® solution is applied with a sterile fine paintbrush. Sterilize the paintbrush by immersion in 70% ethanol for 00:15:00 , and dry by aspiration with vacuum. Ideally, choose a paintbrush with short and square bristles.

After UV sterilization, turn the hood back on, and remove the PBS by aspiration with a glass Pasteur pipette and vacuum. Make sure to aspirate all of the liquid from the VELCRO ® anchors, which are quite absorbent. Then, leave the plates in the incubator for approximately 01:00:00 to dry the plates completely.

Apply Pluronic ® solution according to Figure 5 . Ensure that the region is completely covered, by dipping the paintbrush into the solution and reapplying several times if needed. Figure 5. Region for application of Pluronic ® coating.

Once all plates are coated, leave the dishes in the incubator ( 37 °C and 5 % (v/v) CO 2 ) for 01:00:00 . Importantly, during this time, the coating solution will completely evaporate, leaving only the solute on the surface. After this, it is not necessary to aspirate or wash the coating solution; the hydrogel is directly seeded onto the plates. In this way, the plates will remain completely dry at the time of seeding, which will enable correct spreading of the hydrogel as shown in Step 14.5 .

After two days in maintenance medium, switch the cells to differentiation medium . In Figure 9 , the composition of differentiation medium for AB1079 cells is shown. This medium is prepared using a 3:1 mixture of DMEM and M199, respectively. Agrin is used for mimicking neural signaling for AChR clustering. 6-Aminocaproic acid (6-ACA) is used as an antifibrinolytic agent, which aids in the long-term maintenance of the structure. Figure 9. Differentiation medium for AB1079 myoblasts. References of used materials: DMEM 41966: DMEM Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #41966 M199: M199 medium Fisher Scientific Catalog #MT90050PB Glutamine: L-Glutamine (200mM) Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #25030024 Insulin: Insulin from bovine pancreas Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #I6634-50MG (CAS: 11070-73-8) FBS: Fetal Bovine Serum qualified heat inactivated Brazil Gibco - Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #10500064 Agrin: Recombinant Rat Agrin Protein R&D Systems Catalog #550-AG-100 P/S: Penicillin-Streptomycin Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #P4333 Fungizone: Amphotericin B Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #15290026 6-ACA: 6-Aminocaproic acid Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #A7824-100G Change half of the medium every 2 days (or right before and after a weekend), over the course of 14 days. 336:00:00 . To prevent evaporation, keep muscle construct dishes inside a larger Petri dish (with lid) containing a small dish filled with sterile water.

Prepare a thrombin stock solution according to manufacturer's instructions, using Thrombin from bovine plasma Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #T4648 . Prepare a stock of 100U/ml, to be frozen in individual aliquots. Then, on the day of seeding, dilute these aliquots 1:5 in HBSS ( HBSS, no calcium, no magnesium, no phenol red Thermo Fisher Catalog #14175046 ) to obtain a 20U/ml solution.

steps.title: Prepare PDMS Glue
steps.instruction: Mix Sylgard 184 Dow Corning components at a 10:1 ratio (10 parts elastomer to 1 part curing agent) in a plastic cup. Mix thoroughly with a glass rod until opaque and full of bubbles, then leave in a vacuum dessicator for 01:00:00 to remove bubbles.

substeps.instruction: Store bulk glue at -20 °C if not used immediately.
Bring to room temperature or heat in a 37 °C water bath to reduce viscosity before use.

steps.title: Prepare Petri Dishes
steps.instruction: Mark a 1.2 cm line in the center of each 35 mm ∅ Petri dish using a permanent marker (a paper or plastic stencil is recommended).

substeps.instruction: Optional: Erase marker lines with 70% ethanol after preparation to avoid interference with microscopy.

steps.title: Prepare Velcro Anchors
steps.instruction: Cut arrow-shaped pieces from white VELCRO ® (loop/soft part only, no adhesive backing).

substeps.instruction: Use a pencil to divide VELCRO ® into 12 x 4 mm strips.
Fold and cut strips in half.
Cut arrowheads as per Figure 1B.

steps.title: Attach Anchors to Dishes
steps.instruction: Attach the VELCRO ® anchors to the Petri dishes using the marked center line as a guide.

substeps.instruction: Dab PDMS glue onto the underside of the VELCRO ® pieces using a small spatula.
Place pieces on the lines using tweezers, ensuring tips and the start of the arrowhead regions are aligned.
Leave plates at room temperature overnight to cure the glue.

steps.title: Prepare Cell Suspension
steps.instruction: Trypsinize cells according to standard procedures and collect in a flask.

substeps.instruction: Count cells from an aliquot and calculate the volume needed to obtain 3·10^6 cells per muscle bundle.
Place the calculated volume into individual Falcon tubes.
Centrifuge cells at 800 rpm for 00:05:00.

steps.title: Seed Muscle Bundles
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in a hydrogel (components per Figure 6), keeping all components on ice.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate supernatant and resuspend pellet in 150 µL fibrinogen; keep on ice.
Add 120 µL Matrigel ® and homogenize gently by pipetting.
Prepare a P1000 pipette set to 300 µL.
Add 30 µL thrombin solution and swiftly homogenize 4-5 times with the P1000 pipette.
Aspirate the entire volume and transfer to a Petri dish.

steps.title: Distribute Hydrogel onto Anchors
steps.instruction: Quickly distribute the hydrogel-cell mixture onto the VELCRO ® anchors following the order in Figure 7.

substeps.instruction: Add part of the solution to both anchors, pressing the pipette tip repeatedly to push liquid into the loops.
Add most of the remaining solution to the middle part to connect the two anchors.
Distribute remaining hydrogel around the anchors to cover all sides.

steps.title: Assemble Stimulation Device
steps.instruction: Construct a stimulation device by attaching two graphite rods (bound to copper wires) to the lid of a 35 mm ∅ Petri dish through two small holes, sealing with Loctite ® Super glue.

substeps.instruction: Connect the device to an electrical pulse generator (e.g., Aim TTi TG2512A) and an oscilloscope via a T-adapter and alligator clips.

steps.title: Sterilize Stimulation Device
steps.instruction: Sterilize the device on the day of stimulation if necessary.

substeps.instruction: Place the lid on a 35 mm Petri dish filled with 70% ethanol for 00:15:00.
Wash 3 times with sterile H 2 O.
Sterilize under UV light for 00:15:00 with the electrode part facing upwards.

steps.title: Load Fluo-4 AM for Calcium Imaging
steps.instruction: Add Fluo-4 AM to a final concentration of 10 µM in pre-warmed phenol red-free DMEM.

substeps.instruction: For each dish, use 2 mL of medium and 20 µL of Fluo-4 AM stock solution (1 mM in DMSO with 20 Mass/% volume Pluronic ®).
Incubate for 01:00:00.
Wash cells three times with pre-warmed phenol red-free DMEM (Thermo Fisher Catalog #21063029).
Deesterify by leaving cells in phenol red-free DMEM at room temperature for 00:15:00, then at 37 °C for 00:15:00.

steps.title: Perform Electrical Stimulation
steps.instruction: Stimulate muscle bundles (after 14 days differentiation) using the pulse generator.

substeps.instruction: Program pulse generator: Pulse duration 10 ms, Frequency 1 Hz, Amplitude 10 V (monophasic). Adjust voltage (5-20V) or duration (2-10 ms) based on cell line.
Focus microscope at 20X magnification on the exterior edge of the bundle with the lid off.
Place the electrode lid onto the dish in a safety hood, electrodes parallel to the bundle, and fasten the plate to the stage.
Attach graphite electrode cables to the pulse generator and tape cables to the stage.
Start video recording. After 00:00:10 of no stimulation, turn on the generator for 00:00:50, then turn off and return cells to incubator.

steps.title: Perform Chemical Stimulation
steps.instruction: Stimulate muscle bundles using ACh and KCl solutions.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the Petri dish contains 3 ml of medium; replace if evaporated.
Prepare solutions: ACh (1:100 dilution, 30 µL via P100 pipette) and KCl (1:10 dilution, 300 µL via P1000 pipette).
Set microscope: 20X magnification, 100ms acquisition time (10 fps), 70-80s exposure time, blue light (LED source recommended).
Start recording and add chemical solutions quickly but steadily next to the recorded region according to the chosen regimen (Figure 19 or 20).

steps.title: Perform Optical Stimulation
steps.instruction: Stimulate ChR2+ human myoblasts (after 14 days differentiation) using a coolLED pE-300 system.

substeps.instruction: Program pulse generator (Arduino-UNO™ or PulserPlus): Pulse duration 5 ms, Frequency 20 Hz, Train duration 1 s ON and 1 s OFF, Total duration 1 min (30 repetitions).
Set microscope to brightfield: 1024x1024 px, 16-bit, 40 fps (25 ms/image), exposure < 25 ms, 20X objective.
Start recording. After 00:00:10 of no stimulation, turn on the generator for 00:00:50, then turn off and return cells to incubator.

steps.title: Analyze Contractions with MuscleMotion
steps.instruction: Process brightfield videos using the MUSCLEMOTION plugin for ImageJ.

substeps.instruction: If using .vsi files, open with Bioformats Importer and save as .tif 'Image Sequence'.
Run MuscleMotion plugin, select the correct frame rate, and specify input/output directories.
Extract contraction and contraction speed data from the resulting text files for graphing (e.g., in GraphPad Prism).

steps.title: Analyze Calcium Transients
steps.instruction: Process Fluo-4 AM videos in ImageJ to obtain ΔF/F 0 data.

substeps.instruction: Identify stimulation onset frames by playing the video.
Use the ROI manager and polygon selection tool to outline 5-10 cells of interest; save the ROI set.
Set measurements to 'Mean gray value' only and use 'Multi Measure' to extract fluorescence for all ROIs at each timepoint.
Export results to a spreadsheet.
Create a Z-projection ('Average Intensity') of the video and select a background ROI to obtain the basal fluorescence value (F 0).
Normalize ROI data to F 0 to calculate ΔF/F 0.
Generate an XY plot of ΔF/F 0 over time (X: time in 100 ms increments; Y: ΔF/F 0) using software like GraphPad Prism or Veusz.

description: Check that the muscle bundles detach from the plate within the first 1-3 days of culture. When seen from the side, the muscle bundles should be slightly lifted from the Petri dish as shown in Figure 10 . Figure 10. Detachment of muscle bundles from the Petri dish. During differentiation, take brightfield images of the muscle bundles at 4X and 10X magnification. With these images, perform a directionality analysis to show alignment of cells. This can be done in ImageJ with the Directionality plugin, which will provide a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) of the image, and a directionality histogram ( Figure 11 ). Figure 11. Directionality analysis of a brightfield image corresponding to cells differentiated for 14 days. In order to confirm that differentiation has taken place, perform immunostaining of two key markers: Myosin Heavy Chain (MHC) and acetylcholine receptors (AChR). The latter are relevant if it is desired to perform chemical stimulation with acetylcholine. After staining, perform confocal imaging of MHC and AChR. It is recommended to view both of these markers at 40X magnification. Figure 12. Confocal slice of MHC staining (green) at 40X magnification. Nuclei (blue) stained with Hoechst 33342. Figure 13. Confocal slice of AChR cluster staining (orange) with BTX-Alexa Fluor 555 at 40X magnification. Nuclei (blue) stained with Hoechst 33342 (1:200). Fix the cells with phosphate-buffered paraformaldehyde (PFA) 4 Mass / % volume at Room temperature in a fume hood. First, add one volume of 4% PFA directly to the cell culture medium, to obtain a final concentration of 2% PFA. Incubate for 00:10:00 , aspirate, and fix for 00:30:00 to 01:00:00 in 4% PFA. After fixation, wash thoroughly with PBS (3 times) before taking the plates out of the fume hood. Do not fix cells on ice to avoid depolymerization of Matrigel ® .
